title: Priority surge ledger and tenant sculpting — notes
body:
Overview:

This is a working note for a lightweight approach to handling short-term demand spikes across Dedicated pools that combines (1) a small, append-only priority ledger for surge entitlements and (2) a tenant-sculpting policy layer to shape how capacity is exercised and recovered. The goal: predictable degradation, measurable economics, and simple operator UX for bursty customers without wholesale prewarming.

Why this idea?
- Many customers have intermittent high-priority traffic (feature launches, nightly jobs) that should get preference for a bounded window rather than long-lived reserved capacity.
- Pure credit/burst buckets or pure soft-eviction models both have shortcomings: credits are opaque to operators; soft-eviction can cascade. A ledger gives an auditable trail and a simple reconciler for repairs.

Core concepts
1) Priority Surge Ledger (PSL)
- Append-only ledger entries: {tenant, priority-class, start_ts, ttl_sec, requested_cores, decay_policy, reason} (we'll keep schema minimal initially).
- Each entry is a signed pledge (issued by controller) that represents a short-term entitlement to request a portion of headroom.
- Ledger is authoritative for transient precedence ordering when capacity is contended. Older entries may degrade via decay_policy.

2) Tenant Sculpting
- Local per-tenant shaping that maps PSL entitlements into concurrency slots with three channels: foreground (low-latency), mid (best-effort with latency SLO), background (batch/backfill).
- Sculpting rules decide how many tokens each channel can consume concurrently and apply backpressure to client connections.

3) Soft Overspill Exchange
- When PSL requests exceed capacity, a fallback negotiation runs: candidate entries can be partially honored (split across channels) or requeued into a temporary soft-queue with exponential backoff.
- Exchange publishes a deterministic fallback plan so downstream services can gracefully degrade.

Operator-facing primitives
- API: /psl/pledge (create ledger entry), /psl/status (query ledger view), /psl/relinquish (operator revoke), /psl/reconcile (audit-run)
- Console: a timeline view of pledges, real-time headroom meter, and tenant heatmap.

Customer/SDK primitives
- Optional SDK helper that creates short-lived pledges for high-priority calls (e.g., ad-hoc generation) including reason string. If pledge fails, SDK can fall back to retry policy.

Config knobs (initial set)
- pledge_max_ttl_sec: 1800 (max 30m by default)
- per_tenant_foreground_share: 0.1 (fraction of pool dedicated to foreground non-prefetch traffic)
- surcharge_policy: {priority-class -> cost-multiplier}
- decay_window: sliding window that reduces pledge weight linearly over TTL

Metrics & SLOs to track
- pledge_accept_rate (per-priority-class)
- pledge_overlap_conflicts (number of contention events resolved by ledger arbitration)
- sculpting_throttles_per_tenant
- graceful_fallback_rate (requests that moved to mid/background channels)
- operator_revocations (audit signal)

Runbook sketches
- Normal: pledges accepted and honored. If headroom drops below safety_margin (config), the orchestrator starts preemptive reconcile (reduce pledge weight by decay aggressor factor).
- Contention: system runs deterministic LRU+priority ordering on ledger, then attempts partial honors per soft-overspill exchange. Notify tenants with SLA footprint delta.
- Failure: if ledger sync fails between control plane replicas, fall back to deterministic time-window policy (last N minutes). Alert SRE.

Backward compatibility and migration
- Start as opt-in for tenants: enable ledger in tenant config. No change to default scheduling path until enabled.
- Phase 1: telemetry-only mode (no enforcement) for 2–4 weeks to validate signals.
- Phase 2: enforcement with soft-overspill and surcharge visible in billing.

Economic model ideas
- Charge a small surcharge for pledges above free_quota to discourage abuse. Surcharge is tied to pledge TTL and priority-class.
- Offer pre-packed pledge credits for enterprise customers (better unit price).

Open design questions (TODO):
- How to set per-tenant foreground_share fairly without punting to complex auctions? (suggestion: proportional to commit tier + recent steady-state usage)
- Do we allow cross-pool pledges (e.g., replicate pledges into standby pools)? Latency/consistency tradeoffs must be considered.
- Ledger retention: how long do we keep completed/expired pledges (audit vs storage cost)? Suggest 90d compressed, 14d hot window.

Experiments to run
- Telemetry-only rollout: enable pledge_accept_rate metric for top 30 tenants and compare predicted vs actual headroom pressure during feature launches.
- Small cohort: 5 tenants with SDK integration to exercise /psl/pledge with TTL 5–15 minutes. Measure fallback rates and operator revocations.

Implementation notes for runtime/infra
- Keep ledger lightweight: treat as append-only log in the control plane; store compacted index in Redis for quick arbitration queries. Avoid strong cross-region consensus on first pass.
- Sculpting is local to node-level admission controller (fast path). The admission controller consults cached PSL slices refreshed every 5s.

UX and messaging
- Console language: "Temporary priority pledges" and "Surge sculpting". Emphasize auditable trail and graceful fallback.
- SDK: surface a clear response when pledge is partially honored so app can choose fallback route.

Checklist (immediate next steps)
- [ ] Create Confluence spec page and link design diagrams (Owner: Maya)
- [ ] Prototype ledger schema and a reconcile tool (Owner: Liam)
- [ ] Identify top 30 candidate tenants for telemetry-only pilot (Owner: Omar)
- [ ] Draft billing model and legal review for surcharge (Owner: Priya)

Notes to self / half-baked ideas:
- Could attach a tiny ML predictor to decide whether to accept a pledge by forecasting next 10m tail-latency and heatmap occupancy. Might be overkill.
- Consider an emergency expander token (operator-issued) that temporarily elevates a pledge for high-value outages.

References:
- See linked Jira DED-4812 for initial implementation tasks.
- See Confluence page for mockups (linked above).

Unresolved: definition of "safety_margin" across heterogeneous GPU sizes and quantization profiles. Need an ops primer to map logical cores to physical slot counts.
